name: Xuefuda (oral Chinese preparation, studied only within a multi-part regimen)
short: One study, 40 people with hemophilic arthritis on a multi-part regimen that included Xuefuda: no complications after 215 joint punctures; normal liver, kidney and blood tests. Not tested alone.
text: The only source is a 2007 study from China of 40 hospitalised people with hemophilic arthritis. Xuefuda, an oral Chinese preparation whose ingredients the abstract does not give, was one part of a regimen that also included a haemostatic mixture given into a vein, the antibiotic clindamycin and, for later stages, joint injections of another preparation or of sodium hyaluronate; the abstract states that 'coagulation factors III and IV' (as printed) and blood plasma were not given. Because everything was given together and the abstract describes no comparison group (it says only that the patients were 'hospitalized randomly'), the results cannot be attributed to Xuefuda. Adverse reactions were evaluated: no infection, bleeding or worsening pain followed the 215 joint punctures, and liver and kidney function, electrolytes, ECG, blood glucose and routine blood and urine tests were normal throughout the course; the authors conclude that the treatment was without any adverse reaction but give no event counts. Patients then took Xuefuda for 6 months of consolidation after discharge; the abstract reports relapses for that period but no safety data. No interaction data were found in the cited source.
